question: Why is every even perfect number a power of two times a Mersenne prime?
answer: Every even perfect number splits into a power of two, 2^(p−1), times a prime of the form 2^p−1. The page's rectangle shows this: drag the pearl to change p and check whether the divisors fill the rectangle exactly. Nothing outside this form works.
move: Every even perfect number is 2 p−1 times a prime of the form 2 p −1, and nothing else works.
